summary: This paper proposes an unconventional nonadiabatic geometric quantum computation (UNGQC) scheme for implementing crosstalk-robust two-qubit gates in tunable-coupler superconducting systems by introducing parametric degrees of freedom ($\delta$ and $\varphi$) that steer evolution along optimized trajectories on the Bloch sphere. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the scheme achieves $>99.7\%$ fidelity for controlled-phase gates while suppressing ZZ crosstalk errors and maintaining robustness against qubit frequency drift, even under realistic conditions including decoherence and high-frequency oscillation terms.
motivation: Tunable-coupler architectures offer improved scalability by alleviating frequency crowding, but conventional implementations face a fundamental trade-off: increasing coupler frequency suppresses ZZ crosstalk ($\xi_{ZZ}$) but reduces effective coupling strength $g_e$, forcing longer gate times that accumulate decoherence errors. Previous control schemes addressing this require complex pulse shaping or auxiliary resources.
method: The authors introduce a trajectory-optimization approach based on geometric phases, allowing evolution along triangle-cap paths in Bloch-sphere parameter space (characterized by polar angle $\chi$ and azimuthal angle $\xi$) rather than fixed longitude paths. By varying $\chi$ from 0 to $\pi$ and optimizing detuning ($\Delta_e$) and phase ($\varphi_e(t)$) parameters, they identify the geometry with minimal crosstalk sensitivity ($\chi=0.43\pi$), achieving $g_e/2\pi\sim 4.3$ MHz and gate times reduced by tuning $\omega_c$.
result: For $U_T(\pi)$, $U_T(\pi/2)$, and $U_T(\pi/4)$ gates under realistic conditions with $\kappa=2\pi\times 2$ kHz decoherence, the UNGQC scheme improves fidelity by $\sim 0.7\text{--}1.4\%$ over conventional geometric and dynamical schemes, with numerical validation showing validity of second-order approximations ($\phi_{AC}\ll 1$) to within $0.01\%$ difference from full Hamiltonian simulations.
